script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Romance
Theme: friendship

Begin screenplay.

---

FADE IN:

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

A small, quaint coffee shop in the heart of a bustling metropolis. The aroma of freshly brewed coffee wafts through the air, mixing with the chatter of customers.

At a corner table, JANE (mid-20s, bookish, glasses) sits engrossed in a book. Her face lights up as she turns a page, a smile playing on her lips. Across the room, RICH (late 20s, rugged, charismatic) enters, his eyes scanning the room for a familiar face.

---

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

JANE
(looking up, surprised)
Oh! I'm sorry, I didn't see you come in.

RICH
(smiling)
No apologies necessary, Jane. I'm just glad I found you.

JANE
(startled)
You know my name?

RICH
(leaning back in his chair)
We've met before, at the library. You were helping that little girl with her homework. I couldn't help but notice.

JANE
(blushing)
I see. I'm Jane, by the way.

---

EXT. PARK - DAY

Jane and Rich walk through the park, the sun casting long shadows on the ground. They chat easily, laughing at each other's jokes and sharing stories.

RICH
So, Jane, what do you do when you're not buried in books?

JANE
(laughs)
I teach elementary school. It's rewarding, but it can be exhausting.

RICH
(smiling)
That's impressive. I admire people who dedicate their lives to helping others.

---

INT. COFFEE SHOP - NIGHT

Jane and Rich sit at the same corner table, surrounded by the soft glow of the coffee shop lights. The evening crowd has thinned out, leaving them alone in the quiet space.

JANE
(looking thoughtful)
You know, Rich, I've never really had a close friend. I've always poured my energy into my work and my students. But you... you make me want to be a better person.

RICH
(touched)
Jane, I value your friendship more than you know. And I believe in you. You're an amazing teacher, and an even better person.

---

EXT. COFFEE SHOP - NIGHT

As they leave the coffee shop, Rich takes Jane's hand in his. They walk down the dimly lit street, their steps in sync.

JANE
(looking up at Rich)
Thank you for being there for me, Rich. I don't know what I'd do without you.

RICH
(smiling)
You'd be just fine, Jane. But it's nice to know that I can make a difference in your life.

---

INT. JANE'S APARTMENT - DAY

Jane sits at her kitchen table, grading papers. The phone rings, and she picks it up.

JANE
(on the phone)
Hello?

RICH (V.O.)
Hi, Jane. I was wondering if you wanted to grab lunch with me today.

JANE
(smiling)
Absolutely, Rich. I'd love to.

---

EXT. PARK - DAY

Jane and Rich sit on a bench under the shade of a tree, enjoying their lunch together. They talk about their dreams, their fears, and their hopes for the future.

RICH
You know, Jane, I've been thinking. I want to start my own business, something that will make a difference in people's lives.

JANE
(smiling)
That's wonderful, Rich. I believe in you.

---

INT. CLASSROOM - DAY

Jane stands in front of her class, her eyes filled with pride and joy as she watches her students learn and grow. Rich sits in the back, watching her with a warm smile.

RICH (V.O.)
You're an amazing teacher, Jane. I'm so glad I got to see it firsthand.

---

EXT. COFFEE SHOP - NIGHT

Jane and Rich sit at their corner table, their hands intertwined. They share a tender kiss, their eyes filled with the promise of a lifelong friendship and love.

FADE OUT.

---

THE END
